learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic concepts of thermodynamics such as temperature, work, heat, entropy, efficiency, and the main laws of thermodynamics.
They can characterize the states of systems using state variables and mathematically describe state changes and represent them in diagrams.
Students know the most important processes and understand their fundamental consequences for the design of heat engines and other energy conversion apparatuses.

syllabus_topics: The ideal gas and the incompressible liquid as model fluids
The principle of energy conservation, the 1st Law of Thermodynamics
Carnot cycle as an ideal reference process
Thermodynamic cycles (Joule cycle, Clausius-Rankine cycle, Otto cycle, Diesel cycle)
assessment_rules: The module final examination (Klausur) has a duration of 150 minutes and accounts for 100% of the module grade. To receive credit points, the module final examination must be passed. In the exam, students are expected to characterize system states using state variables and mathematically describe and diagram state changes.
